records.note: Comparative efficacy claim (semaglutide works better than naltrexone and topiramate for alcohol use disorder) with no benchmark: no trial, metric, effect-size threshold or data series is named. A comparative without a benchmark is VAGUE. Writing a trial_result event would require inventing a trial the forecaster did not name. 'Probably' would be bin B if admitted.

Eulogy tribute: 'his work and ideas will evolve into a stunning set of treatments'. No entity, observable event or threshold can be written; 'a stunning set of treatments' is a slogan. Paraphrase of a Philip K. Dick letter adopted as the author's own words, so not THIRD_PARTY.

Compound eulogy claim ('one hell of a commercial success' and 'become the standard of care') for the treatments Nolan Williams envisioned (SAINT/SNT, ibogaine). Neither part has a benchmark: no revenue figure, series, guideline body or adoption threshold. Both parts fail the same test, so one record, not a split. 'In the future' is not a deadline. The author's employer Radial offers SAINT-type care, which would make the item affiliated if it were admitted.

Own-organization expansion: Radial (the author is Chief Medical Officer) will 'soon' open clinics in St. Louis, MO and Chattanooga, TN. Clinic openings by the forecaster's own company are commitments, not forecasts. 'Soon' is not a deadline.

Hope that journalists' training on suicide reporting is changing and that media coverage of suicides will improve. Media reporting practice is not a regulatory, clinical-trial, company or market, payer or policy, or practice-adoption outcome. Also framed as a wish ('I certainly hope') and 'improve' has no benchmark. Republished 2022 text.

Present-tense belief about efficacy: 'Spravato and ketamine are both effective' in the right patients, and one underpowered study (KARMA-Dep 2) does not change the author's view. No future state is asserted and no future trial, meta-analysis or decision is named. 'I suspect' would be bin B if a forecast were present.

Population-health statistic: the author doubts the 2025 high-school suicide-attempt rates are better than the 2023 figures he cites (13 percent of girls, 7 percent of boys). Adolescent suicide-attempt prevalence is not one of the five areas. The claim is otherwise well formed as a quantity direction call on a national youth survey series with 'this year' = 2025-12-31 and 'I doubt' = bin D with asserts false; logged here for the record.

Denial that chatbots or antidepressant drugs will 'fix' high adolescent suicide-attempt rates. 'Fix' has no threshold, no data series and no period, so no quantity event can be written; the intervention classes ('a chat bot', 'drugs') have no defined set. Compound claim, both parts fail the same test, so one record. 'Not gonna' would be bin E if admitted.

Workforce claim: there will 'never' be 'enough' therapists or child psychiatrists. 'Enough' has no benchmark, no headcount threshold and no named workforce series. Compound claim, both parts fail the same test, so one record. 'Never' is not a deadline.

Hedged efficacy belief: accelerated TMS 'might work' for adolescent depression, paired with the normative 'we should run the studies'. No trial, sponsor, endpoint or effect-size threshold is named, so a trial_result event would require inventing a trial. The remark that once-daily TMS 'probably works' and already has an FDA label is descriptive, not a forecast.

Own-event announcement: the author organizes the RAMHT live newsletter event series and announces the next one (RAMHT-AI) for 11 January 2026. Whether the event happens is the forecaster's own decision. Also outside the five areas.

'More kids will get more effective treatment for their depression' after the FDA cleared the BrainsWay H1 coil for adolescents. The quantifier 'more' has no countable set, no series and no period, so no quantity event can be written. The finder's CONTROL reading is not taken: the claim is about adolescents in general, not Radial's own action, but the author's employer Radial provides deep TMS, so the item would be affiliated if it were admitted.

'More [GLP-1 drugs] coming soon': a pipeline call with no product, company, regulator or decision named. The quantifier 'more' has no countable set and 'coming soon' names no observable event (approval, launch, trial). 'Soon' is not a deadline.

Childhood sexual abuse prevalence (20 percent of girls, 5 percent of boys) restated in future tense, marked by the author as a restatement of an earlier claim. Population prevalence of abuse is not a regulatory, clinical-trial, company or market, payer or policy, or practice-adoption outcome. Also descriptive rather than a forecast.
Joke closing about an internet outage: 'I'm sure it will be working again in no time'. Internet service is outside the five areas. Joke framing; 'in no time' is not a deadline.

Own-event announcement: RAMHT 2026 SF live event on 11 January (2026) in San Francisco, organized by the author. Restates the date given in owen-1948 but in a different post, so not DUPLICATE. Also outside the five areas.

Own-event announcement: the fifth RAMHT live event on 11 January (2026) in San Francisco, organized by the author. Third mention of this date in the packet, each in a different post, so not DUPLICATE. Also outside the five areas.

'The next step, of course, is broad insurance coverage' for accelerated dTMS and adolescent dTMS (BrainsWay). No payer, program, policy or code is named and 'broad' has no countable set, so the coverage_decision template cannot be filled without inventing a payer. Paired with an exhortation to call health plans, HR and government. The author's employer Radial delivers dTMS, so the item would be affiliated if admitted.

Section heading 'The Psychedelics Are Here...Almost.' over MindMed MM-120, COMP360 psilocybin and AtaiBeckley 5-MeO-DMT data. 'Here' names no observable event (approval, launch, availability) and 'almost' is neither a probability phrase nor a deadline. Slogan; no event can be written without inventing the outcome type.

'Insurance coverage still lags, I'm looking at you, 2026': an exhortation about coverage of rapid-acting treatments. No payer, treatment code, policy or threshold is named, so no coverage_decision or quantity event can be written. '2026' would anchor to 2026-12-31 if an event existed. No probability phrase.

Market-size opinion: 'more than enough suffering for the number of companies above and more' (Radial and eight competitors). No metric, revenue figure, survival event or series; 'more than enough' has no benchmark. Not read as a survival forecast for the listed companies. The author is Radial's Chief Medical Officer.

'This makes the treatment scalable and thus accessible to more people who need it' after FDA clearance of accelerated and adolescent dTMS (BrainsWay). The quantifier 'more' has no countable set, series or period; present tense with only an implied forward reading.
Own-newsletter content plan: the author is sure he will write about cohort studies again. The forecaster's own action; also outside the five areas.
Eulogy claim that Nolan Williams' 'love and rigor will be saving lives for years to come'. No entity decision, observable event or threshold can be written. 'For years to come' is not a deadline.
Own-newsletter series plan: this post is the first of 'Owen's Letters to the Health Professionals' and more are implied. The forecaster's own action; also outside the five areas.

Generic advice to prescribers that some relationships will end, ex-partners will seek revenge and 'your professional license will be used against you'. Personal relationships and generic human behaviour are outside the five areas. The quantifiers 'some' and 'reliably' also have no countable set.

Generic clinical claim that untreated severe trauma is 'not gonna work itself out on its own reliably'. No entity, trial, cohort, metric or threshold is named, so no observable event can be written. Statement about the natural course of illness, not a forecast of a decision or result.

Own-organization launch: 'We are bringing a depression treatment device to market soon', disclosed as Neurolief, where the author is an executive and advisor. Bringing a product to market is the forecaster's own organization's action. Any implied FDA clearance is not stated as a claim. 'Soon' is not a deadline.

Paradigm claim: Flow Neuroscience's FDA approval of at-home tDCS is 'the death-knell for daily drug-first or daily drug-only biological treatment for depression as a paradigm'. No metric (prescriptions, market share, guideline change), threshold, series or period is named, so no quantity or rule event can be written. Slogan.
Editorial thesis: 'medical devices that modulate the brain is the future'. Slogan with no observable event, benchmark or set; restates a long-running editorial stance.

'The sham will need to be improved to preserve the blind in future trials': a requirement statement ('will need to be' = must) about trial design after functional unblinding in the EMPOWER tDCS trial. No predictive reading that a specific sponsor or trial adopts a better sham; no trial named.

Negative expectation that tDCS will not deliver SAINT-level results ('we shouldn't expect that from tDCS'). A comparative without a benchmark: no future tDCS trial is named and no effect-size threshold for 'SAINT-level' is given in the forecaster's words (only the Flow trial's 0.37 is cited). 'Shouldn't expect' would be a predictive-should denial if an event existed.

Own-organization vision statement in the Radial launch post: 'We see a future where psychiatric treatments work'. Slogan; no entity decision, observable event or threshold can be written. The author is Radial's Chief Medical Officer.
Generic collaboration prediction: people across the rapid-acting treatment companies 'will be working together both before and after whatever job we have'. No observable event, set or benchmark.

Radial press release republished by the author as 'our press release': the Series A 'will support the company's plans to expand nationally in 2026'. National expansion of the forecaster's own company is a commitment, not a third-party outcome. 'In 2026' would anchor to 2026-12-31 in the commitments table.

Radial press release: 'The company is building a national network of clinics that accept most major forms of insurance'. The forecaster's own company's build-out; present progressive with only an implied forward reading. 'Most major forms' has no countable set.

Radial press release marketing claim: for patients the best therapies 'are available to everyone who needs them', for payers 'better outcomes and less ultimate cost'. No payer, metric, cost series, threshold or period is named, so no quantity or coverage event can be written. Own-organization promotional text.

Quote attributed to John Capecelatro, Radial CEO, inside the company press release the author republishes as 'our press release'. Read as adopted (the author is Radial's Chief Medical Officer); the adopted claim, 'Radial is here to change that' so people access therapies 'far sooner', is the forecaster's own organization's commitment with no benchmark. If adoption is not accepted, THIRD_PARTY applies instead; the item is rejected under either reading.

The author's own quote in the Radial press release: 'We're taking what we know from years of clinical research and turning it into care that any patient can access'. Own-organization mission claim; Radial's own action. 'Any patient' has no countable set.
Personal memoir statement: the author will never know whether his sister's overdose was intentional. Personal knowledge, outside the five areas; no third-party decision or observable event.
